question.prompt:
In the figure below, \(3\) of the \(6\) disks are to be painted blue, \(2\) are to be painted red, and \(1\) is to be painted green. Two paintings that can be obtained from one another by a rotation or a reflection of the entire figure are considered the same. How many different paintings are possible?

[Figure 1](figures/2017_AMC_12B_Q13_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The single green disk gives a useful way to organize the count. In the triangular arrangement, it can occupy either a corner position or a position between two corners. Rotations carry any position of one type to any other position of that type, but no symmetry interchanges the two types.

First fix the green disk at one chosen corner. Choosing the two red disks from the five remaining positions determines the entire painting, because the other three disks must be blue. There are
\[
\binom52=\frac{5\cdot4}{2}=10
\]
red selections before identifying mirror images.

Any symmetry identifying two paintings with green at this fixed position must keep that position in place. Besides doing nothing, the only such symmetry is reflection across the line through the green disk and the opposite side disk. Among the five remaining positions, this reflection fixes one position and swaps two pairs of positions.

A red selection unchanged by reflection must contain both members or neither member of each swapped pair. Since there are exactly two red disks and only one fixed position, the selection must be one complete swapped pair. There are exactly two such selections. The other eight selections form four distinct mirror pairs. Hence the number of paintings in this case is
\[
2+\frac{10-2}{2}=6.
\]
Now fix green at one chosen position between corners. The remaining reflection again fixes one of the other five positions and swaps two pairs. The same count therefore gives six paintings.

These cases include every painting, and they do not overlap because a symmetry cannot change the green position from a corner to a side position. Thus the total is
\[
6+6=\boxed{12},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Fix the green disk and pair mirror images
